chunks: A group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Yaqoub ibn Yaqteen, who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! The Dhuhr prayer arrives, but we are not able to descend (from the upper floor) during the time until they descend, and we descend with them, so we pray. Then they stand and hasten, so we stand and pray Asr, and we show them as if we are bowing (in ruku'). Then they descend for Asr, so they place us in front, and we pray with them.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Pray with them, may Allah not send blessings upon them.'

key_terms.لَا صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ: May Allah not send blessings upon them (a formula of distinction)

ai.seo_question: How should Shia Muslims pray with general Muslims when their prayer times overlap?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of praying behind Ahl al-Sunnah when necessary, emphasizing that the validity of the prayer is not compromised by the Imam's specific status. The Imam’s instruction to pray with them while mentally or ritually distinguishing the act via the declaration 'Lā ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhim' reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of avoiding unnecessary hardship (rukhas) while maintaining theological distinctiveness. This ruling is particularly significant in contexts where Shia Muslims are a minority and must join general congregations for Dhuhr or Asr.
